title: About
text:
About the Author
This project was created by Alexa Titherington as a final data science project at New College of Florida.

Contact: a.titherington30@ncf.edu
GitHub: github.com/alexajt
Project Repository: github.com/alexajt/national-parks



Data and Purpose
This project uses NPS-reported annual recreation visits to compare visitation across units and years. The 2000–2025 dataset contains 9,612 park-year records from 400 units. Counts represent reported visits, not unique people; reporting units and counting methods can vary. Data: NPS IRMA Stats Portal and NPS Visitor Use Statistics Dashboard.

text:

title: National Park Visitation Through the Years
text:
Key Takeaways (2000–2025)




Recreation Areas & Parkways


1.09M


Median annual visits across 44 units (1,109 observations). Open scenic parkways and shorelines lead the system in typical volume.






National Parks & Preserves


520K


Median annual visits across 76 units (1,953 observations). Flagship natural parks draw sustained crowds, with leaders exceeding 10M visits.






Historic Sites & Memorials


113K


Median annual visits across 208 units (4,922 observations). Over half of all reporting units preserve focused historical and memorial heritage.






National Monuments


97K


Median annual visits across 72 units (1,628 observations). Protects landmark geological, archaeological, and cultural sites across the nation.

title: Visitation Shifts After 2020
text: The 2020 pandemic triggered sharp, uneven disruptions across the National Park System. Open outdoor destinations like scenic parkways and flagship national parks rebounded quickly—surpassing pre-pandemic benchmarks by 2025. In contrast, urban monuments and historic sites took deeper hits and still trail 2019 attendance by roughly 14%. Below, trace the category-wide recovery trajectories followed by the individual park units with the largest post-2019 volume shifts.
